title: Project wine data onto principal components
description: You inspect variance ratios, a two-component projection, and feature loadings.

steps.description: You center X and compute its singular value decomposition. Squared singular values give component variances, which you divide by their sum to get explained variance ratios.
You request two principal components for the wine data and retain the full variance-ratio array. The first plot shows cumulative explained variance across all components.
You plot the first two projected coordinates and use yw to color the observations. The axes identify PC1 and PC2.

steps.question: How does top_loadings choose which six features to print for each component?
steps.answer: It sorts the absolute component weights in descending order. It prints the selected weights with their original signs.

steps.description: You read the largest feature weights for each direction, called loadings. The recorded PC1 list begins with flavanoids at -0.423, and PC2 begins with color_intensity at -0.530.
